```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
library(sciparseR)
ex <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "sciparseR")
```

## Figures

A figure is located from its caption and the ink on the rendered page:
the region above (or below) the caption that holds drawing or image ink
and no body text. Vector graphics count as ink, so charts drawn as PDF
paths are found too.

```{r}
fe <- sc_parse(ex("figure_equation.pdf"))
sc_figures(fe)[, c("figure_id", "label", "page", "x0", "y0", "x1", "y1", "method", "caption")]
```

`sc_figure_crop()` renders the page and writes the figure region as PNG.
The checksum of the source file is verified first, so a crop always comes
from the file that was parsed.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("png", quietly = TRUE)}
f <- sc_figure_crop(fe, sc_figures(fe)$figure_id[1], tempfile(fileext = ".png"), dpi = 100)
dim(png::readPNG(f))
```

Cropping is not digitization: sciparseR does not read values off plots or
reconstruct Kaplan-Meier curves.

## Equations

Display equations are found as centered lines with a right aligned label
such as "(1)". From a PDF, only the text of the equation is available:

```{r}
sc_equations(fe)[, c("label", "text", "latex", "latex_status")]
```

`latex_status = "not_reconstructed"` says that no LaTeX was produced. The
characters are there (Greek letters and operators as Unicode), but the
two dimensional structure of fractions, sums and scripts is not recoverable
from text positions alone, so sciparseR does not pretend to rebuild it.
From JATS, the TeX and MathML of the source are kept
(`latex_status = "source_markup"`).

## References

The reference section is found by its heading. Each entry is parsed with
patterns for the common numbered (Vancouver) style; the identifiers DOI,
PMID and PMCID are extracted wherever they appear.

```{r}
doc <- sc_parse(ex("single_column.pdf"))
sc_references(doc)[, c("ref_id", "label", "authors", "year", "journal", "volume", "pages", "doi", "pmid", "pmcid")]
```

Fields that cannot be read with confidence stay `NA`; the full reference
text is always kept in `text`.

## Citations

Numeric citations, including ranges and lists ("[2,3]", "[4-6]") and
superscript numbers, are expanded and linked to references by label.
Author year citations are linked when the first author and year match
exactly one reference.

```{r}
sc_citations(doc)[, c("citation_id", "block_id", "marker", "ref_id", "char_start", "char_end", "style", "status")]
```

The offsets point into the block text, so the citation can be shown in
context:

```{r}
ci <- sc_citations(doc)[1, ]
txt <- doc$blocks$text[doc$blocks$block_id == ci$block_id]
substring(txt, ci$char_start, ci$char_end)
```

## Footnotes

Page footnotes (marked with symbols or numbers at the bottom of a page)
and table footnotes are separate entities with a `scope`:

```{r}
doc$footnotes[, c("page", "scope", "marker", "text")]
```

## Comparing with GROBID

GROBID is an excellent dedicated tool for references and header
metadata. It is not required, and sciparseR never calls it, but if you
run it yourself you can compare its TEI output with sciparseR's result
using `sc_read_grobid()` and `sc_compare_grobid()` (see
`vignette("ocr-models-grobid")`).
